This method enhances physical resilience while sharpening mental focus, creating strength from the inside out.

mark_story.title: Meet Mark
mark_story.paragraph1: Hello! I'm Mark Oogan, a 56-year-old Irishman who's called Sweden home for the past 20 years. My journey in fitness began early, as a semi-professional cyclist in Ireland for five years in my teenage years. I then delved deep into martial arts – Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu, Karate, and Boxing – fueling a lifelong passion for sports. My vision for Bonobo Gym truly crystallized after training with Jon Hinds at Monkey Bar Gym in Darwin, Australia, where I became a certified natural trainer. This experience shaped my core belief: train the body as a single, integrated unit, focusing on natural strength, coordination, and mobility.
mark_story.paragraph2: At Bonobo, a big part of our philosophy is that training must be enjoyable. Sometimes that means fun warm-up games, but it always means keeping things stimulating, mentally and physically. While we incorporate standard strength training with weights, reps, and time intervals – the essence of any good gym – what truly sets us apart is our commitment to weaving coordination, rhythm, and mobility into every single workout. Every class includes a dynamic warm-up, often with playful games, a main workout, and a dedicated stretch after. This consistent format ensures a holistic and engaging experience for everyone.
mark_story.image_alt: Mark Oogan, founder of Bonobo Gym, smiling.

maja_story.title: Meet Maja
story: Movement and wellness have been central to my life for as long as I can remember.

I competed in skiing and rhythmic gymnastics throughout my youth, and after retiring from competition in my late teens, I naturally transitioned into teaching. I spent 10 years instructing aerobics and step aerobics before discovering Pilates, which I went on to teach for another decade.

After moving to Sweden six years ago, I discovered Soma Move, a practice that immediately resonated with me. I became certified and began teaching it alongside other modalities. Today at Bonobo, I lead the MVMT class—a blend of my favorite techniques and disciplines, rooted in one guiding principle: respecting and listening to our bodies.

My approach focuses on building strength, improving mobility, and preventing injury. We work with isometric holds, muscle fatigue (with adjustments), and a whole-body perspective. Equally important is knowing when to push and when to slow down. That awareness—learning to tune into your body and move with intention—is at the heart of everything I teach.

Each class ends with a meditative cool-down, creating space to carry calm and presence into the rest of the day. I really like the approach focused on helping us to live a fit, injury-free life, grounded in self-awareness, and kindness (and some fun along the way:)
And absolutely love being part of Bonobo community

features.name: Joy in Movement & Unrivaled Community
features.description: Our trainers – Mark, Maja, Christian, and all others – share a universal enthusiasm for movement. We infuse playfulness into every session, believing that fitness should be fun, even when it's challenging. This creates a powerful sense of community. Our members consistently tell us how friendly and welcoming everyone is, making it easier to step through the door and feel right at home. We foster strong bonds, often gathering for social events outside of classes, like our famous Irish Coffee workout at Christmas!

features.name: All Levels Welcome, Always Adjustable
features.description: Whether you're a seasoned athlete or have never trained before, our classes are designed to be adaptable to your individual level, age, or any physical limitations. Our coaches provide hands-on guidance, ensuring you're challenged appropriately. You'll always be pushed to your maximum, safely and effectively.

features.name: Results-Driven & Integrated Coaching
features.description: Don't be fooled by the fun – our workouts are hard work! We specialize in strength and conditioning, constantly nudging you to lift heavier, get stronger, and improve your overall fitness. The small group setting allows our trainers to provide personalized coaching, knowing your capabilities and helping you progress. This blend of community and individualized attention ensures you get the most out of every session, driving real, tangible results.

questions.question: What should I wear to a class?
questions.answer: Comfortable athletic wear and supportive indoor training shoes are recommended. For Movement classes, some prefer to train barefoot or in socks.

questions.question: Do I need to book in advance?
questions.answer: Yes, all classes must be booked in advance through our online system to ensure your spot, as our small group classes have limited capacity.

questions.question: What if I have an injury or physical limitation?
questions.answer: Please inform your coach before the class begins. Our experienced trainers are skilled at providing modifications and alternative exercises to ensure you can participate safely and effectively at your own level.

questions.question: How early should I arrive for my first class?
questions.answer: We recommend arriving 10-15 minutes before your first class to allow time for a quick registration, meet your coach, and get settled.

questions.question: Is there parking available?
questions.answer: Limited street parking is available directly outside the gym.

questions.question: What happens in an introduction consultation?
questions.answer: The consultation is a short conversation with Mark about your goals, training history and best next step. It can lead to a membership, HumanTrak movement profile, PT, or a class recommendation.

questions.question: Can I bring a friend to train with me?
questions.answer: Our Gold and Gold+Coach members can bring a friend who is not currently a member to our monthly 'Friend Friday' event. Other passes do not include this perk.

questions.question: Can I freeze my membership?
questions.answer: Yes! Our Silver membership includes a 2-week freeze per year, and our Gold and Gold+Coach memberships include a 4-week freeze (split into two 2-week periods). Please contact us to arrange a freeze.

questions.question: What is your cancellation policy?
questions.answer: Our monthly memberships can be canceled at any time with 30 days notice. Class packs, bootcamps, and annual memberships are non-refundable.

questions.question: Are there options for kids?
questions.answer: Yes, we offer a Children and Youth Pass which is valid for our specific classes for younger members. Please check the class schedule for details or contact us for more information.

questions.question: What if I have never trained before?
questions.answer: No problem! Our classes are designed for all fitness levels. Our expert coaches will provide modifications to ensure you get a safe and effective workout.

measure.title: One platform, three practical use cases.
measure.description: HumanTrak is a portable markerless 3D movement-analysis system. At Bonobo, the technology supports coaching: it helps identify training priorities and gives each person or group a baseline to retest against.
measure.source_intro: Based on official VALD product and support information:

items.title: Mobility
items.description: Range-of-motion tests for shoulders, trunk, hips, ankles and other key movement areas.

items.title: Balance
items.description: Standing balance and control tests for general adults, athletes and active-aging clients.

items.title: Symmetry
items.description: Left-right comparisons reveal where training may need more attention.

items.title: Reports and retesting
items.description: A tangible report and repeatable test battery help turn training progress into proof.

process.title: How the Lab works
process.description: Every path follows the same simple loop: measure, choose priorities, train, then retest.

steps.title: Baseline
steps.description: Run a test battery matched to the person, team or workplace.

steps.title: Three priorities
steps.description: Translate the results into the most useful training focus areas.

steps.title: Training plan
steps.description: Connect the result to classes, PT, team work or workplace follow-up.

steps.title: Retest
steps.description: Repeat the same tests in 8-12 weeks to see what changed.
